text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet proposed to raise tenfold capital requirements for licensing insurance firms in a move to provide a stable insurance market, Justice minister Vassil Gotsev said.
-- Bulgaria raised natural gas prices by five percent effective from today, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 362 billion levs in May to 2.9 trillion levs, a Bulgarian National Bank senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's private Orel G insurance holding company said it would raise its capital to six billion levs in line with draft amendments to the Insurance law proposed by the cabinet.
-- Bulgaria's state National Electricity Company (NEC) said it would raise electricity prices by 10 percent from July 1. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to replace armed forces Chief of Staff general Tsvetan Totomirov by Air Force commander Miho Mihov, introducing a principle to rotate commanders of army, air and naval forces as heads of armed forces Chief of Staff.
-- A major shipyard in Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas went on strike demanding higher wages and replecement of management, trade union officials said.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had chosen the offer of Belgium's Union Miniere SA for a 56 percent stake in Bulgaria's state MDK copper smelter. @

-- A mission of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) lead by the IMF executive director for the group of countries including Bulgaria Johannes Wijndholds discussed the progress of structural reforms in the country with Prime Minister Ivan Kostov.

-- Bulgaria's biggest military hardware plant Vazovski Mashinostroitelni Zavodi (VMZ) said it would go on strike on June 18 demanding higher wages after talks with VMZ management were deadlocked last week.

-- A leak of gasoline vapors at one of the compressors of Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim in Bourgas caused a fire which was extingished by a local fire squad, refinery officials said. No victims were reported. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
